entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Al-Hasan ibn Sahl was a prominent Abbasid official and governor of Iraq, serving under Caliph al-Ma'mun during the Fourth Fitna (821-833 CE).

Born in unknown circumstances, Al-Hasan ibn Sahl rose to prominence as a skilled administrator and diplomat, playing a key role in maintaining the stability of the Abbasid Caliphate in the face of internal strife and external threats. His tenure as governor of Iraq was marked by significant economic growth, infrastructure development, and cultural achievements, cementing his legacy as one of the most important figures of the Abbasid era.

Despite his many accomplishments, Al-Hasan ibn Sahl's life was cut short by his untimely death in 851 CE, leaving behind a lasting impact on the history of Iraq and the wider Islamic world. His influence can still be felt today, with many historians and scholars continuing to study and debate the significance of his life and reign.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, Al-Hasan ibn Sahl remains a vital figure in the annals of Islamic history, offering a unique window into the complexities and challenges of life in the Abbasid Caliphate during its most tumultuous period.
